title: Practice setup, photos and wrapping up the session

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: So you've been all in all keeping quite active.
You don't have a set of drums in the apartment, do you?
I didn't see it. Can you practice here? Do the neighbors hassle you at all?
Oh yeah..... I think we've got a nice little session going for the two days, don't you?
I think so, yeah. We were just looking at Cozy's rogue gallery.
Which is pretty impressive, which has photos going all the way back to his childhood and going through his days with Wilbur Sweatman and on and on and on.

And he was also showing me his practice setup which he's got kind of, it's a trap set up with a set of practice pads and cymbals that are carefully taped up and enable him to practice to his heart's content.
Much to the envy of a horn player like myself who has to contend with neighbors all the time.

Yes, I know. But that's one reason why I like this apartment I have, as you see it's on the ground floor, it doesn't bother with anybody and I've got my little tapes and my little record players, my little earphones in there and I can just get in there and get my chops up good and wail until I fall out. And that's what I enjoy and it's my life and I'm so happy that I can do it, and I have a place such as this where I can practice like this and not annoy anyone.
